requirements.title: Derived-type operations require explicit generic function definitions
requirements.source: 7.5.11 p1, second and third sentences; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF 109.
requirements.definition: The document specifies no intrinsic operations on derived-type entities. Any operation on derived-type entities must be explicitly defined by a function and a generic interface.

pending.no-intrinsic-derived-operation-fallback: PENDING source-control plan: type box has integer component x. The conforming program adds only a generic OPERATOR(+) interface and function before evaluating a+b; the source-control variant removes that generic and is nonconforming without assigning a diagnostic obligation to this prose unit.
pending.explicit-generic-function-operation: PENDING runtime plan: module interface OPERATOR(+) maps to add_box(left,right). For left%x=2 and right%x=3, add_box returns result%x = left%x*10 + right%x, so a+b must produce 23. A plain function call add_box(a,b) is a companion control and does not by itself define the operator.

requirements.oracle: The operator plan uses exact integer component values and a sentinel result 23 that intrinsic assignment, component copying, or reversed operands would not produce. The nonconforming source-control variant is retained only to document the boundary; no rejection facet is claimed here.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This prose shall constrains programs but is not a numbered constraint, so this catalogue does not create a mandatory diagnostic facet. Generic resolution, operator syntax, and procedure interface details remain owned by clauses 10 and 15.
requirements.dependencies: Confirmed existing owner catalogues opened: doc/catalogues/defined_operations_15_4_3_4_2.json, doc/catalogues/generic_interfaces_15_4_3_4.json, doc/catalogues/generic_identifiers_15_4_3_4_1.json, and doc/catalogues/derived_types_7_5_10.json. Expression/operator interpretation in clause 10 remains a dependency.

requirements.title: Derived-type defined assignment requires an explicit generic subroutine definition
requirements.source: 7.5.11 p1, third sentence; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF 109.
requirements.definition: A defined assignment for derived-type entities must be explicitly defined by a subroutine and a generic assignment interface; intrinsic assignment remains governed by 10.2.1.

pending.explicit-generic-subroutine-assignment: PENDING runtime plan: interface ASSIGNMENT(=) maps to assign_box(lhs,rhs). Starting lhs%x=-5 and rhs%x=7, execute lhs = rhs and expect lhs%x=107 because the subroutine stores rhs%x+100. The distinct -5 sentinel proves the left side changed through the explicit generic assignment path. A separate intrinsic-assignment control without the generic copies x=7 under 10.2.1.

requirements.oracle: The assignment plan uses exact integer values. The 107 sentinel distinguishes defined assignment from ordinary component copy of 7 and from an unchanged left side of -5. The intrinsic-assignment control keeps the cross-reference separate from the defined-assignment requirement.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source unit supplies no mandatory rejection oracle for a missing or malformed generic assignment interface. Detailed dummy-argument characteristics and assignment interpretation remain owned by clauses 10 and 15.
requirements.dependencies: Confirmed existing owner catalogues opened: doc/catalogues/defined_assignment_statement_10_2_1_4.json, doc/catalogues/defined_assignments_15_4_3_4_3.json, doc/catalogues/generic_interfaces_15_4_3_4.json, and doc/catalogues/intrinsic_assignment_statement_10_2_1_2.json. Name resolution in clause 19 remains a dependency.

accounting.rationale: J3/24-007 PDF 109: paragraph subdivided into the intrinsic-assignment cross-reference, operation requirement, and defined-assignment requirement.
J3/24-007 PDF 109: cross-reference to 10.2.1 for intrinsic assignment of derived-type entities; the executable intrinsic-assignment semantics are owned by clause 10.
